studies.name: ABCD Study
studies.note: Waves are item-level where the public ABCD 7.0 dictionary gives REDCap branching logic (1,124 items with event conditions). All other items keep table-level coverage, which can over-state waves for items added later (e.g. youth social-media and video-game addiction items).

studies.name: LSAC (Growing Up in Australia)
studies.note: Full Release 10.1 dictionary (77,039 variable × wave rows, B and K cohorts, W1–W10 incl. between-wave mail-outs). Wave = data file (cohort × child age); variables are aggregated across waves on their age-free stem. Informant from the dictionary "Person Label": Study Child = Y, Parent 1/2, mother, father, parent living elsewhere = P, teacher/carer = T, derived scores = D. Construct = keyword screen plus LSAC's own construct labels (e.g. Electronic gaming, Social media use, Media supervision, Parental warmth, Hostile parenting, Parental monitoring).

studies.name: AStRA (Athens)
studies.note: Dictionary rebuilt from the three SPSS output files. Ages: C1 (2005–07) and C2 (2013–15) start in the first grade of Gymnasium, M age 12.6 at W1 (Motti-Stefanidi et al., 2017, N = 1,057 and 1,052), with annual waves (≈12.6, 13.6, 14.6); C3 (2022–23) spans Gymnasium grades 1–3 at W1 (≈12–15). No screen-time items in C1–C2; C3 has internet-quality and parent–adolescent conflict over computer/phone time.

studies.name: Trondheim Early Secure Study
studies.note: Instrument overview (English): 150 rows × 11 columns (instrument label + 10 time points, T1 4y to T10 22y); 683 of 1490 time-point cells filled. Every row now carries a cell for each time point, so instruments are placed at the correct wave and age. Digital media: screen-use interview (T3–T10), Internet Gaming Disorder Interview (IGDI, T4–T10), semi-structured clinical IGD interview (T4–T8; Wichstrøm et al., 2026, Addiction), social media use (T4–T10), FoMO (T7–T10), cyberbullying (T6–T10) and objective 7-day app time-use screenshots (T7–T10). Retrospective objective app-use records matched to each wave are confirmed by the study lead but not itemised in the overview; data-donation streams (social media and AI interaction records) are planned. Item-level wording still needs the TESS codebook.

studies.name: Growing Up in Ireland
studies.note: Cohort '24 not yet in the variable list.

studies.name: Growing Up in New Zealand
studies.design: Birth cohort (born Apr 2009–Mar 2010); antenatal → 6 weeks → 9m … 8y, 12y, 13y e-wave, 15y
studies.note: Full data dictionary: 43 tabs (data collection wave × informant: M mother, P partner, CM/CP parent report on the child, C child self-report from 8y, CO observation, T teacher), 16035 variables. Ages are the scheduled collection ages; fieldwork years are approximate windows from the birth cohort. The crosswalk rows used before have been replaced.

studies.name: KCYPS 2018 (Korea)
studies.design: E4 (≈10y) and M1 (≈13y) cohorts in 2018; annual W1–W7
studies.note: Ages are approximate, from school grade. Constructs are identified through the Korean scale names of the KCYPS 2018 questionnaires (e.g. 부모양육태도 – 구조제공, 스마트폰 의존, 삶의 만족도), bridged to the English dictionary, plus the English keyword screen. KCYPS 2018 has no parental-monitoring (knowledge/supervision) or media-rules scale; the closest is parenting Structure (구조제공: rules, expectations, explanations), shown under monitoring as a proxy. The Korean codebook (NYPI) would allow item-level Korean matching.

studies.name: Panel Study on Korean Children
studies.dict_file: PSKC SPSS files W1–W16 (Korean variable labels)
studies.note: Item level from the Korean variable labels of all 16 public SPSS files (21235 variables; metadata only, no participant values). Constructs found with a Korean term lexicon (data/korean_construct_terms.csv), e.g. 부모 감독 → parental monitoring, 스마트폰/미디어 이용 → screen time, 게임 → gaming, 우울 → low mood, 행복감 → wellbeing. Item text is shown in Korean. Informant from the questionnaire letter (J child, E/F/D mother/father, I/L school/teacher, A assessment). The lexicon needs review by a Korean speaker.

studies.name: Ten to Men
studies.dict_file: Ten to Men 2025 Release Data Dictionary.xlsx
studies.note: Includes adult men; youth slice = boys cohort. W2 years not stated in the dictionary (verify).

studies.name: Understanding Society (UKHLS)
studies.design: Household panel: BHPS 1991–2008, UKHLS 2009– (W1–W15); youth 10–15, adults 16+; Innovation Panel, COVID-19 Study, PEACH
studies.note: Targeted harmoniser dictionary (condensed from the 50,067-stem full dictionary to the 11 Atlas constructs): 1433 item × construct rows, 958 variable stems, across UKHLS main survey, harmonised BHPS, Innovation Panel, COVID-19 Study, PEACH, IP Wellbeing App and the IP Twitter linkage. Informants: Y youth self-completion 10–15, P parent/proxy about the child, A adult self-report (youth slice 16–25 at analysis), H household, S linked Twitter/X data. Adult items were screened by keyword only, so rarely worded adult items may be missing. BHPS waves before 2000 are listed in Atlas and Item compare but not plotted on Two clocks.

studies.name: HILDA
studies.note: Youth slice (15–24) to be defined at analysis. Child items come from one adult (household questionnaire).

adii.about: Australian Digital Inclusion Index (ADII): adult (18+) population index, 0–100, across Access, Affordability and Digital Ability. Two series that must not be spliced: the legacy Roy Morgan series (2014–2020) and the Australian Internet Usage Survey series (2020 pilot, 2021, 2022, 2024). The 2024 Affordability measure was redesigned, so 2024 totals are not comparable with earlier totals. The current AIUS series surveys adults 18+ only (the legacy series reports an age 14–24 band), so ADII describes the household and parental digital environment of Australian cohort members (LSAC, HILDA, Ten to Men), not the young person’s own use.
adii.cite: Thomas, J., McCosker, A., Parkinson, S., Hegarty, K., Featherstone, D., Kennedy, J., Ormond-Parker, L., Morrison, K., Rea, H., & Ganley, L. (2025). Measuring Australia’s Digital Divide: Australian Digital Inclusion Index 2025. ADM+S Centre of Excellence for Automated Decision-Making and Society, RMIT University, Swinburne University of Technology, and Telstra. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
adii.link: Join to cohort records by data year × state/territory × capital city vs rest of state × remoteness area (data year, not publication year). Geography-only joins as the primary analysis; subgroup-matched scores (e.g. couple with children × income quintile) as sensitivity analyses.
